pool.note: First-impression manners keyed by category; every line is colour.

rows.text: Efficient, slightly distracted: someone with too many things in their head and a practised way of not showing it.
Warmer than their office suggests. They have the gift of making people feel briefly important.
Formally polite. Every sentence is measured before it leaves their mouth.
Tired. Not rudely, but visibly. This is a person who has been doing a hard job for a long time.
Direct. They assess you in the first three seconds and their expression tells you they've reached a provisional conclusion.
Professionally cordial: the manner of someone who deals with strangers all day and has a system for it.
Relaxed in a way that reads as confidence rather than carelessness.
Alert. Not hostile, but attentive in a way that doesn't quite switch off.
Genuinely glad to see you, or performs it so well the difference doesn't matter at first.
Composed. The particular stillness of someone who has practised being still.
Interested in you as a person, or at least in what you might need. The attention feels real.
Watchful, in a religious way: not suspicious, but as though taking a reading.
Quick to smile, quick to calculate. Both things are happening simultaneously.
Busy, or presenting as busy. The first impression is of someone who doesn't waste time.
Affable. The manner of someone for whom friendliness is both genuine and useful.
Cautious with newcomers. The wariness is professional rather than personal.
Unremarkable, deliberately. The kind of person you would walk past twice.
Helpful in a way that asks for nothing obvious in return. Yet.
Friendly, easy, slightly too interested in where you're from.
Quiet. They let other people fill the silence.
Elsewhere, mentally. The conversation is happening in the foreground while something else has most of their attention.
Precise: words chosen carefully, pauses before answering, a slight sense of being assessed.
Unexpectedly approachable. Whatever you expected, this isn't it.
Polite but removed. Not unfriendly, just operating at a different register.
Ordinary in a way that is itself a kind of presence.
Open. The impression of someone with nothing in particular to hide, or who has decided not to hide it.
Tired, but alert. The combination of someone who works hard and pays attention.
Reserved. Not hostile, just private.
